title: Minerva Mills v. Union of India

content.caseIdentity: Minerva Mills v. Union of India, (1980) 3 SCC 625
content.facts: Minerva Mills, a textile undertaking in Karnataka, had been nationalised under the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974. The petition challenged provisions connected with the Forty-second Constitutional Amendment, particularly provisions that expanded Parliament's amending power and restricted judicial review.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether the constitutional provisions inserted or altered by Sections 4 and 55 of the Forty-second Amendment could remove limitations on Parliament's amending power
Whether the challenged provisions damaged the basic structure by excluding judicial review or disturbing the constitutional balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles
content.ratioDecidendi: The power to amend the Constitution is limited by the basic structure doctrine. An amendment cannot convert the limited amending power into an unlimited one or destroy judicial review and the constitutional balance between Parts III and IV.
content.holding: Sections 4 and 55 of the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act were severed and struck down for violating the basic structure, leaving the rest of the amendment intact.
content.relevance: Reinforced that limited amending power, judicial review, and the constitutional balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles are protected by the basic structure doctrine.
